title: Specimen Preparation, Imaging, and Analysis Protocols for Knife-edge Scanning Microscopy
protocol: Anesthetize C57BL/6J mouse using isoflurane inhalant anesthesia.
Decapitate the anesthetized mouse.
Place the brain into a Golgi-Cox fixation solution.
Incubate the brain in the Golgi-Cox solution in the dark, at room temperature, for 10 to 16 weeks.
Rinse the brains in deionized water overnight in the dark.
Immerse the rinsed brain in 5% ammonium hydroxide solution in deionized water for 7 to 10 days in the dark at room temperature.
Rinse the brain again in deionized water at room temperature for 4 hours.

Dehydrate the brain through a graded series of ethyl alcohols: 50%, then 70% (both in the refrigerator at 4 °C), followed by 85%, 95% (three changes) and 100% (four to five changes, all in room temperature).
Soak the brain in acetone for three to four days.
Place the brain in an araldite-acetone mixture with ratios of 1:2, 1:1, and 2:1, each for one day in the refrigerator at 4 °C.
Submerge the brain in 100% araldite (three changes) overnight in the refrigerator at 4 °C.
Embed the treated brain in 100% araldite and heat to 60 °C for 3 days.
Transfer specimens embedded in LR White from the last 100% ethanol solution through three changes of LR White solution kept overnight in the refrigerator.
Transfer specimens to fresh LR White and polymerize at 60 °C for 24 hours.
Mount the cured specimen block on a metal specimen ring using epoxy.
Trim the sides of the mounted block as necessary.
Deeply anesthetize the mouse using ketamine and xylazine injected intraperitoneally.
Perfuse the transcardially with 50 mL of room temperature phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4).
Perfuse with 250 mL of cold 4% phosphate-buffered paraformaldehyde (pH 7.4).
Perfuse with 100 mL of a solution of 0.1% thionin dye in deionized water.
Place the body in the refrigerator at 4 °C for 24 hours.
After 24 hours, remove the brain from the calvaria and place it in a fresh solution of 0.1% thionin.
Store the brain at 4 °C for 7 days to ensure full infiltration of thionin into the en bloc preparation.
Begin destaining and dehydrating the brain through a graded series of ethanols starting with 50% ethanol and water, increasing to 100% ethanol over a period of 6 weeks.
Store changes from 50% to 70% ethanol in the refrigerator (4 °C).
Store all changes above 70% ethanol at room temperature.
Change the brain through three acetone solutions (2-4 days in each solution at room temperature).
Embed the brain in araldite plastic following the protocol outlined.
If using LR white as the embedding medium, follow the protocol specified for it.
Deeply anesthetize the mouse using ketamine and xylazine injected intraperitoneally (1.7 mg ketamine / 0.26 mg xylazine per 20 grams body weight).
Perfuse the mouse transcardially with 50 mL of room temperature phosphate-buffered saline.
Perfuse the mouse transcardially with 250 mL of room temperature 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Perfuse the mouse transcardially with 3.0 cc of undiluted India ink to fill the vasculature completely.
Turn off pump.
Turn on stage.
Turn on camera.
Turn on illuminator.
Raise knife and objective.
Install specimen ring.
Measure specimen dimension and create a configuration file for the KESM Stage Controller2 application.
Start KESM Stage Controller2 and initialize stage.
Lower knife/objective.
Turn on pump.
Focus objective and camera by turning the focusing knob on the optical train.
Adjust the camera's field of view relative to the knife edge.
Press [Go] to initiate imaging.
Copy the KESM Stack Processor executable into the data folder under the configuration file folder.
Run the KESM Stack Processor to remove lighting artifacts and normalize background intensity in all images.
Repeat for all data subfolders.
Prepare multiscale tiles from the dataset.
Upload and set up the files in the KESM Brain Atlas web server.
Go to http://kesm.cs.tamu.edu and select the appropriate atlas.
Navigate as in Google maps.
Zoom in and out as in Google maps.
Select how deep to go at each step from the pull-down menu, then click on either [+] or [-] to increase or decrease z depth.
Adjust the overlay number by using the pull-down menu.
Adjust the overlay interval by using the pull-down menu.
Launch MeVisLab.
Create a new project.
Type in the module name [Compose3Dfrom2DFiles] and go to the desired folder.
Enter file string and click on [GetFileList].
Make sure the selected images can fit in memory.
Click [Create3D] to create volume.
Create module [SetWorldMatrix].
Set "Scale" under "Elementary Transforms" x, y, z to the appropriate voxel size (0.6, 0.7, 1.0 for a 10X 0.45NA objective).
Link [Compose3Dfrom2DFiles] to [SetWorldMatrix].
Set Matrix and Transforms under "Matrix Composition" to "Ignore", "Ignore", "Forward".
Create module [Arithmetic1] and set the "Function" to "Invert(Max-Img)".
Link [SetWorldMatrix] to [Arithmetic1].
Create module [View3D] and connect [Arithmetic1] to it.
While right mouse button is pressed in View3D, move the mouse around to adjust the threshold.
Crop regions as needed.
Change orientation by moving the mouse while left mouse button is pressed.
Change illumination between volume rendering and MIP.
Turn on or off background as required.
